$comment: Rule catalog — test integrity. Standard 47. Hidden skips route to Standard 30 R3 and Standard 28 R5, which already refuse to count a skip as a pass.

rules.title: Tests are not weakened or removed to make a build pass
rules.description: No legitimate test is deleted because it fails, no assertion is loosened to make a build green, and no coverage is reduced to satisfy CI. A demonstrably incorrect test may be changed, with the demonstration recorded before the change.
rules.rationale: The qualifiers are internal to the prohibition, so no exception can be legitimate: anything the rule still forbids is a suite adjusted until it agreed with the code, which makes a green run meaningless.
rules.remediation: Restore the assertion and fix the defect. Where the test was genuinely wrong, record which requirement it contradicted before changing it, and treat any moved behaviour as a scope change.
rules.$assuranceNote: Not automatable: the violation is a claim about WHY a test changed. Test removal is detectable in principle but needs history analysis this framework does not do.

rules.title: Test results are not claimed without execution
rules.description: No test result, build result, or compilation result is reported for a run that did not happen, and no output is invented for one.
rules.rationale: There is no supported reason to report the result of a run that did not occur, which is why no exception exists. This is Standard 9 R4 stated as a prohibition, because the failure is a false statement rather than an omission.
rules.remediation: Run the command and report what it printed, or state plainly that it was not run and why.
rules.$assuranceNote: Not checkable from a repository: nothing in a commit distinguishes a claim about a run that happened from one about a run that did not. CI executing the commands itself is the structural defence.

rules.title: Behavioural verification is not replaced by tautologies
rules.description: A test asserts the behaviour of the code under test rather than the behaviour of its own mocks, and mocking does not extend so far that the subject itself is stubbed out.
rules.rationale: A test that cannot fail proves nothing, but the line between a legitimately mocked boundary and a mock that has swallowed the subject is a judgement about what the test was for.
rules.remediation: Mock the boundary, not the subject: replace the external dependency and let the code under test run.
rules.$assuranceNote: A prohibition here would fire on every unit test with a stub or on none, and neither is worth the false confidence.
